name: cloud-libs
description: Ships every constellation library module as its own installable APK.
_doc: ab_cloud-libs-shared/keyboard-engines bundles five modules into ONE companion APK. This repo is the general case: one APK per library module, so each lib is installable, updatable and inspectable on its own. Nothing here names a module - the set comes from scanning lib_apks.scan, so a new module in aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ ships an APK with no edit to this file (FIRE RULE #6).

lib_apks._doc_scan: Every directory under ANY of these paths that contains a build.gradle is a library module and gets an APK. A list because ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs holds every SHARED module (consolidated there 2026-08-30 - it is the only multi-consumer root), while cal/contacts/maps/news/wallet are single-app feature modules that stayed in their own repos. Module names must be unique ACROSS roots - the name is both the gradle path and the applicationId suffix - and settings.gradle fails the build if two roots collide. Paths are relative to this repo's root.
lib_apks._doc_exclude: Modules that must NOT ship as a standalone APK, each with the reason. An exclusion is a claim about install-time behaviour, so it belongs in data next to the scan rule rather than as a silent skip in gradle.

exclude.sysdns: #741 The fleet's one bridge to Android's resolver for code that cannot use it directly (ResolverProxy for the gh, rclone and gix binaries; SystemDnsBridge for terminal shells). A plain library: no component, nothing to install, nothing an app binds. It is compiled into Cloud-Lib-Gh/-Rclone/-Gix here (settings.gradle includes it for them) and into cloud-drive, and the terminal forks compile its bridge source by reference.
exclude.decisions: #772 OpenRouter's Decisions API client (plain JVM Kotlin), compiled by Cloud Calc's Jev section and by Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Image-Mlkit's OpenRouter route. No component, nothing to install, nothing an app binds: it rides inside the APKs that need it.
exclude.fleetconfig-model: #825 The fleet-config manifest + migration policy (FleetPolicy, FleetPolicyEngine), split out of libs:core. No component, nothing to install: it rides inside Cloud-Lib-Fleetconfig (libs:fleetconfig, the engine every app's FleetConfigProvider binds) and the SuperApp, which plans the fleet with it.
exclude.databackend: #825 The generic engine wire (IDataBackend, DataBackendService, DataBackendClient), split out of libs:core. No component, nothing to install: it rides inside every engine APK that extends it and every app that binds one.
exclude.ml-l-sound: #798 The CONTRACT half of sound identification: the ISoundEngine wire, the client and sound.json that Cloud Calc and Cloud Camera compile. It has no component and installs nothing; the engine it binds ships as Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Sound-Yamnet.apk, which compiles this module in.
exclude.disk: #813 The Disk Management engine is #763 `pinned`: it reads other apps' sizes under the usage-access grant and walks/deletes shared storage under the all-files grant of the app that compiles it (cloud-drive). A standalone APK would hold neither grant, so it would install a package that can read nothing.
exclude.disk-scan: #813 libs:disk's arithmetic, plain JVM and PIT-tested. No component, nothing to install: it rides inside cloud-drive through libs:disk.
exclude.sound-tags: #798 The arithmetic of sound identification (WAV decoding, resampling, the model's windows, averaging, the label list a model carries), plain JVM and PIT-tested. No component, nothing to install: it rides inside Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Sound-Yamnet.apk, the only module that compiles it.
exclude.ml-l-image: The CONTRACT half of the image scan (engine-apk-split move 6): the IImageScanEngine wire, the typed payload and the client that Drive, Mail, Camera, Media Center and Office compile. It has no component and installs nothing; the engine it binds ships as Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Image-Mlkit.apk, which compiles this module in.
exclude.cropper: Upstream image-cropper UI for cloud-media-center, moved into the shared root with the rest of its libs/. It was never a lib APK — media-center was not a scan root — and a standalone cropper APK installs nothing anyone can open. Excluded so the shipped set is exactly what it was before the merge.
exclude.gesture: Same: upstream gesture helper, compiled into cloud-media-center only.
exclude.panoramaviewer: Same: upstream panorama viewer, compiled into cloud-media-center only.
exclude.scrollbar: Same: upstream fast-scrollbar, compiled into cloud-media-center only.
exclude.keyboard: Already ships as its own APK (Cloud-Keyboard.apk, ac_cloud-keyboard). A second package carrying the same LatinIME service would register a duplicate input method, and its clipboard/gesture ContentProvider authorities come from string resources that both packages would claim - INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER.

lib_apks._doc_exec_native: #705 Modules whose APK must let Android EXTRACT its native libraries at install. AGP keeps every .so stored uncompressed inside the APK and extracts nothing (measured on the published Cloud-Lib-*.apk, 2026-10-01: libgh.so, libgix.so and librclone.so are all stored), which is right for a library loaded with System.loadLibrary and fatal for a BINARY an engine execs: nativeLibraryDir is the one place an app may exec from on API 29+, and with nothing extracted it is empty, so the engine answers 'gh is not installed' from inside the very APK that carries gh. Listed per module, with the reason, because extraction costs every OTHER lib APK install-time disk for nothing; app/build.gradle applies it to exactly these flavors through the variant API (the same packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging switch cloud-drive sets for its own jniLibs), and a name here that is not a shipped module fails the build. A module whose service execs its own binary and is missing here is refused by test/test-engine-services.sh.

exec_native.gh: #705 GhBackendService execs libgh.so out of this APK's own nativeLibraryDir; Cloud Drive binds that service instead of carrying gh.

lib_apks._doc_ids: Flavor applicationId = <application_id_prefix>.<module name with '-' stripped>; release asset = <asset_prefix><Module-Name>.apk. Derived, never listed.
lib_apks._doc_categories: #642 THE ONE DECLARATION of the Libs tab's tables, in render order. An APP is filed by the launcher's central classification (the section+folder its All Apps grid uses), which is why Cloud ▸ Apps has always drawn headed tables. A LIB has no launcher entry, so that classifier returns nothing for it and all 46 rows fell into one unnamed run - the flat list. This supplies the SAME (heading, order) pair from data instead, so StoreCloudFragment groups libs through the mechanism it already had rather than a second one. Members are FLEET ids (lib-<module>, plus the rows regen.sh adds from elsewhere: keyboard-engines, the two rootfs libraries, ae-tool_termux-boot) - the same shape as constellation.groups.members, so the two lists read alike. Ordering is this array's order; within a table it stays A-Z (#334). FIRE RULE #6 still holds: a new module under ../libs still ships an APK and still appears with no edit here - it lands under 'Other' until someone files it. What regen.sh REFUSES is a member id that is not a lib row, because that is a category quietly pointing at a renamed or deleted module. ML libs are not here: ml-{t|l}-{domain}-{name} already names its own tab (#405). #667 FIXED TWO NAMES AND THE REASONING IS THE POINT, because both were about to be tidied back. (1) There was one 'Shell & Input' bucket holding two unrelated kinds. bottomnav/launcher-apptabs/launcher-onehand/launcher-zoomies DRAW - they are Views and Fragments (BottomNavIslandView, AppTabsFragment, ArcMenu, CircularMenu, PetStrengthView), so they are 'ui'. text-tools/translate/voice/keyboard-engines COMPUTE - engines, engine clients and model management (TranslateEngines, Translator, VoiceEngines, VoiceModelManager) - so they are 'language'. Precisely: translate and voice DO each ship one thin bar the keyboard hosts (TranslateBarView, VoiceBarView); that makes them language engines carrying a host-embedded bar, NOT launcher chrome, which is why they moved. (2) 'Runtimes' was wrong twice over. The rootfs libs are complete userlands (~400MB, see the Libs group blurb) that the terminals proot INTO - an OS image, not a language runtime - and the word collides with its own real meaning, because a runtime like nodejs_22 is a thing that lives INSIDE the rootfs and cannot leave it (#664). So the label is OS. ae-tool_termux-boot stays with them because it is the hook that brings that userland up. Do not rename 'os' back to 'runtime'.

android._doc_abi_filters: Mirrors ab_cloud-libs-shared/keyboard-engines. Only ml-l-voice-vosk/ml-l-text-mlkit carry .so payloads; the rest are unaffected by this filter. Add 'x86_64' for Waydroid/emulator and rebuild - no gradle edits needed.
android._doc_packaging_excludes: Duplicate files that must not reach the APK. This repo packages 29 unrelated dependency sets through ONE wrapper module, so license/notice collisions are the normal case rather than an exception: libs:wallet pulls com.sun.mail:android-mail AND android-activation, which both carry META-INF/NOTICE.md, and mergeWalletDebugJavaResource failed the WHOLE build - one flavor taking all 29 APKs down with it. ac_cloud-wallet has carried the same block for its own APK all along. Data, not gradle, so the next collision is a one-line edit here. Never add *.kotlin_module: dropping those breaks Kotlin reflection at runtime, silently. META-INF/versions/*/OSGI-INF/MANIFEST.MF (a glob, every multi-release level): the mwiede jsch fork ships an OSGi manifest under versions/9 AND versions/15, and so do jspecify (9) and bouncycastle via sshj (15) — measured on runs 36068993994 and 36074399160, 2026-09-24. One level at a time was a chase.
android._doc_no_compress: #798 asset extensions every APK keeps STORED: ML Kit's LocalModel memory-maps a bundled .tflite (the image engine's full-label classifier, data/models.json), which a compressed asset cannot be. Applied by app/build.gradle's androidResources.noCompress for every flavor; only the ML engines carry such files.

tests._doc: #705 Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which ship-cloud-libs.yml runs before it builds. These testers are the ENGINE side of the app/engine split: once an app binds an engine instead of compiling it, the app's own ship no longer watches the engine's directory, so the only pipeline that runs when an engine changes is this one, and the engine's side of the contract is checked HERE or nowhere.

unit._doc: The engines' JVM suites, run through build.sh test (build.entry below) after the workflow has set up the JDK, the SDK and Gradle. :libs:gh's GhLoginTest runs the gh engine's real sign-in job against a fake gh that prints the one-time code and then blocks, and fails unless the code reaches the job while gh is still waiting; it also runs libs:sysdns's ResolverProxy, the loopback tunnel gh needs to resolve names inside an app. #741 :libs:sysdns's own SysDnsTest runs the terminals' DNS bridge against a fake resolver (the client's id comes back, a failed lookup is a SERVFAIL glibc accepts, an oversized UDP answer is truncated there and whole over TCP) and the proxy in the any-host mode rclone and gix use. The phone once showed a DNS failure for a sign-in that never reached GitHub, and no shell tester can execute either property. #798 :libs:ml-l-sound-yamnet's ClassifierTest replays the real YAMNet's scores for a golden clip through the engine's whole pipeline and reads the label list out of the real, sha-verified model file; :libs:ml-l-image-mlkit's DetectorTest does the same for the classifier object detection names boxes with; :libs:sound-tags runs PIT (gate 80). One task per engine that has a suite, space-separated.

build._doc: Read by cloud-android-test-engine.sh's unit phase only: this repo has no gradlew, and build.sh test is the invocation that fetches the pinned firestack aar first, as every gradle run here does.

modules._doc: Only the wrapper lives here. The :libs:* modules are appended by settings.gradle from the lib_apks scan above, each pointing at the one canonical directory in ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR + sops-decrypts the passwords. NO fallback.

release._doc_kind: 'lib' = a companion APK that ships engines/behaviour rather than UI. data/regen.sh files these under the SuperApp Constellation page's Libs tab instead of Apps. This repo produces MANY of them, so regen.sh expands lib_apks into one fleet entry per module.
release._doc_auto_update: libs:updater is itself one of the shipped modules and reads release.auto_update from the CONSUMING repo. Disabled here on purpose: each library APK has its own GHCR image, while the updater carries a single image name, so a self-update would pull the wrong artifact. Library APKs are updated by the SuperApp's Constellation page (Libs tab), which knows each one's asset.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

ghcr._doc_image: Per-module image name is '<image_prefix><module>' - that is what build.sh pushes. `image` is the repo-level fallback that libs:updater's BuildConfig reads; it is never pushed to, because a library APK does not self-update (see auto_update below).
ghcr._doc: DISABLED for the same reason ac_cloud-watchdog disabled it, and it is the fix rather than a workaround. A GHCR package is owned by the ACCOUNT, not the repository: GitHub creates every new user-owned package PRIVATE whatever repo pushed it, image.source only LINKS it, and no API can change it (PATCH /user/packages/... 404s even with write:packages). Measured: cloud-watchdog was deleted and rebuilt by GITHUB_TOKEN from inside this PUBLIC repo's own workflow and came back private. One APK per library module means one package per module, so this flow multiplies the problem: cloud-lib-watchdog 403'd and cloud-lib-search was private too. A channel that cannot follow repo visibility is one these APKs do not ship on; the GH Release asset IS the repo and follows it by construction. Re-enable only under an ORG namespace, where PATCH /orgs/{org}/packages/.../visibility exists.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.
